records.title: Opioid use disorder evidence page
records.summary: Evidence level: early human and observational. Human evidence: Observational detoxification reports, follow-up studies, and registered oral Ibogaine withdrawal research. Main limitation: Durability, relapse denominator data, missing follow-up, concurrent supports, and adverse-event denominator data remain incomplete. Safety: Cardiac risk, concurrent substances, withdrawal physiology, electrolyte issues, psychiatric status, and medication interactions. Not proven: Ibogaine is not proven to cure opioid addiction.

records.title: Traumatic brain injury evidence page
records.summary: Evidence level: limited observational. Human evidence: A 30-person veteran prospective observational study and later neurophysiology work drew attention and require side-by-side design-limit explanation. Main limitation: Small sample, male veteran population, Mexico treatment setting, concurrent supports, selection effects, and short follow-up. Safety: Screening, cardiac monitoring, magnesium context, psychiatric history, and follow-up. Not proven: Ibogaine is not proven as a general TBI treatment.

records.title: Parkinson's disease evidence page
records.summary: Evidence level: no direct human data. Human evidence: A 2026 peer-reviewed case report describes one patient treated with low-dose Ibogaine hydrochloride over 80 days using validated Parkinson's instruments. Main limitation: One-patient evidence is highly uncertain and vulnerable to placebo, expectation, medication changes, and disease variability. Safety: Age, cardiac status, neurological comorbidity, drug interactions, sleep worsening, and medication changes. Not proven: Ibogaine is not proven as a Parkinson's treatment.

records.title: Withdrawal and cravings evidence page
records.summary: Evidence level: limited observational. Human evidence: Withdrawal and craving findings appear in OUD studies, observational detoxification reports, and substance-use reviews. Safety: Withdrawal physiology, dehydration, electrolytes, cardiac risk, benzodiazepines, alcohol, stimulants, opioids, and polysubstance use. Not proven: Craving reduction or withdrawal relief is not the same as a cure.
